title: Beginner
desc: Foundations: to be, present simple, articles a/an, plurals & everyday prepositions.

classes.title: Class 1: To be + word order
classes.desc: am / is / are in positive, negative and question forms / Short answers (Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.)

questions.q: Put in order: is / where / the station / ?
questions.explanation: Question word + be + subject: 'Where is the station?'.

questions.q: "Are you a student?" Which short answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Positive short answers are never contracted (not 'Yes, I'm').
'My brother and I' = we (plural subject), so use 'are'.

questions.q: Put in order: to school / goes / every day / Tom
options: Tom goes to school every day.
Tom goes every day to school.
Every day Tom to school goes.
Tom to school every day goes.
questions.answer: Tom goes to school every day.
questions.explanation: Subject + verb + place + time: Tom goes to school every day.
'Glasses' is always plural in English even though it refers to one item.
English uses 'be', not 'have', when stating age.
The direct object ('music') comes straight after the verb.
Short negative answer for 'she' is 'No, she isn't.'

classes.title: Class 2: This, that, these, those + this vs it
classes.desc: This/these = near; that/those = far / Singular vs plural

questions.explanation: 'These' is used for plural items close to the speaker.
'That' refers to a singular item at a distance.
Plural of 'This is a bus' is 'These are buses'.

questions.q: You hold a pen: "___ is my pen. ___ is a good pen."
questions.explanation: The first mention points ('this'); after that we refer back with 'it'.

questions.q: You point at cars far away: "___ cars are expensive."
questions.explanation: 'Those' is for plural objects far away.

questions.q: On the phone you ask who is calling: "Hello, who is ___?"
questions.explanation: On the phone, you ask 'Who is that?' and introduce yourself with 'This is...'.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "Those is my bag."
questions.explanation: 'Bag' is singular, so use 'That is my bag' (or 'Those are my bags').

questions.q: You hold two shoes: "How much are ___?"
questions.explanation: 'Shoes' is plural and close to the speaker.

questions.q: "Look at that dog. ___ is so big!"
questions.explanation: The dog is already introduced, so refer back with 'It'.

questions.q: "___ is raining and ___ is cold today."
questions.explanation: Talking about weather conditions always uses dummy pronoun 'It'.

questions.q: Do you like ___ photo in my hand?
questions.explanation: A single photo held in hand takes 'this'.

questions.q: Look at ___ stars in the night sky!
questions.explanation: Stars are plural and far away, so use 'those'.

classes.title: Class 3: Pronouns and possessive adjectives
classes.desc: Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they / Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their

questions.q: My parents are here. ___ are nice.
Maria and Tom are friends. ___ live in Paris.
This is my sister. ___ name is Eva.
questions.explanation: Possessive adjective for a female person is 'Her'.
'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive adjective for an animal.

questions.q: "Give ___ the keys, please." (said to you by Anna and me)
questions.explanation: Object pronoun after the verb 'give' is 'us'.
'Anna and I' is the subject of the sentence.

questions.q: I like Sam, but he doesn't like ___.
questions.explanation: Object pronoun after the verb 'like' is 'me'.

questions.q: I know Dan, but I don't know ___ sister.
You and I are friends. ___ are happy.
Tom and Eva have a dog. ___ dog is called Max.

classes.title: Class 4: Whose, possessive 's + have got
classes.desc: "Whose is this?" / "It's Mike's." / 's for one owner, s' for plural owners

questions.q: "These are the girls' coats." How many girls are there?
questions.explanation: More than one. The apostrophe comes after the s (girls').

questions.q: "Peter's got a dog." What does 's mean here?
questions.explanation: has. Peter has got a dog. 's can mean is, has, or possession.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "The childrens' toys are old."
questions.explanation: The children's toys are old. "Children" is already plural, so add 's.

questions.q: The room belongs to two boys. "It's the ___ room."
"Have you got a pen?" "No, ___." (a) I haven't got. (b) I haven't. (c) I don't.
Correct the sentence: "Has you got a pen?"
Rewrite with 's: "the book of my sister"
"These are the girls' coats." How many girls are there?
questions.explanation: More than one. The apostrophe comes after the s (girls').

questions.q: "Peter's got a dog." What does 's mean here?
questions.explanation: has. Peter has got a dog. 's can mean is, has, or possession.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "The childrens' toys are old."
questions.explanation: The children's toys are old. "Children" is already plural, so add 's.

questions.q: The room belongs to two boys. "It's the ___ room."

classes.title: Class 5: A/an, plurals + the / no article
classes.desc: a before consonant SOUNDS, an before vowel SOUNDS / Regular and irregular plurals

questions.explanation: an. The h is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.
a. It starts with a "y" sound (/j/).
knives, teeth, sheep (sheep does not change)

questions.q: "I like ___ pizza. ___ pizza on the table is cold."
questions.explanation: no article, The. In general = no article; a specific pizza = the.
the guitar, no article football. Instruments take "the"; sports do not.
no article. Meals take no article.
an. The h is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.
a. It starts with a "y" sound (/j/).
knives, teeth, sheep (sheep does not change)

classes.title: Class 6: Adjectives + adverbs of manner
classes.desc: Adjectives go before nouns and after "be"; they never change for plural / Adverbs end in -ly (quick → quickly)

questions.explanation: happy. After "look/feel/smell/be" we use an adjective.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "I have two reds cars."
questions.explanation: two red cars. Adjectives do not take -s.

questions.q: I got up ___ this morning, so I missed the bus.
Which is correct? (a) a red small car (b) a small red car

questions.explanation: happy. After "look/feel/smell/be" we use an adjective.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "I have two reds cars."
questions.explanation: two red cars. Adjectives do not take -s.

classes.title: Class 7: Present simple
classes.desc: Present simple for habits, routines, facts / he/she/it + -s / -es / -ies

questions.q: My father ___ (watch) the news every night.
Which is correct? (a) He don't know. (b) He doesn't knows. (c) He doesn't know.
questions.explanation: (c). After doesn't, the verb has no -s.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Does she goes? (b) Do she go? (c) Does she go?
My sister ___ (try) hard and my brother ___ (play) a lot.
questions.explanation: tries, plays. Consonant + y → -ies; vowel + y → -s.

questions.q: My father ___ (watch) the news every night.
Which is correct? (a) He don't know. (b) He doesn't knows. (c) He doesn't know.
questions.explanation: (c). After doesn't, the verb has no -s.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Does she goes? (b) Do she go? (c) Does she go?

classes.title: Class 8: Questions + adverbs of frequency
classes.desc: Order: Question word + do/does + subject + verb / who, what, where, when, why, how, what time

questions.q: Put in order: does / what time / she / get up
options: What time does she get up?
questions.answer: What time does she get up?
questions.explanation: What time does she get up?

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Where she lives? (b) Where does she live? (c) Where does she lives?

questions.explanation: Who. We ask about people with "who".

options: I am sometimes tired on Mondays
questions.answer: I am sometimes tired on Mondays
questions.explanation: I am sometimes tired on Mondays.

questions.q: "How ___ do you go to the cinema?" "Twice a month."
What does "I don't always eat breakfast" mean? (a) I never eat breakfast. (b) I sometimes eat breakfast.

questions.explanation: likes. When "who" is the subject, no do/does is used, and the verb takes -s.

questions.q: Put in order: does / what time / she / get up
options: What time does she get up?
questions.answer: What time does she get up?
questions.explanation: What time does she get up?

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Where she lives? (b) Where does she live? (c) Where does she lives?

questions.explanation: Who. We ask about people with "who".

classes.title: Class 9: Present continuous + present simple or continuous?
classes.desc: am/is/are + verb-ing for actions now / Negatives and questions

questions.explanation: know. "Know" is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Do you working? (b) Are you working? (c) You are working?
questions.explanation: (b). It is a question, so "Are" comes first.

questions.q: Tom usually ___ (wear) a suit, but today he ___ (wear) jeans.

questions.explanation: don't understand. State verbs are not used in the continuous.
is having. Here "have" means eat, so the continuous is OK ("She has a car" would not be).
know. "Know" is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Do you working? (b) Are you working? (c) You are working?
questions.explanation: (b). It is a question, so "Are" comes first.

classes.title: Class 10: The imperative + can/can't
classes.desc: Imperatives: Sit down! Don't talk! / can/can't for ability, possibility, permission

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "She can to swim."
questions.explanation: She can swim. "Can" is followed by the base verb, never "to".
Don't be late. The negative imperative of "be" uses "don't" too.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Do you can swim? (b) Can you swim?
"Can I sit here?" What does it ask for? (a) ability (b) permission
questions.explanation: (b). It is a request for permission, not about ability.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "He cans speak French."
questions.explanation: He can speak French. "Can" never takes -s.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "She can to swim."
questions.explanation: She can swim. "Can" is followed by the base verb, never "to".
Don't be late. The negative imperative of "be" uses "don't" too.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Do you can swim? (b) Can you swim?

classes.title: Class 11: At, in, on (time and place) + position words
classes.desc: Time: at (clock, night), in (months, years, parts of day), on (days, dates) / Place: at (point), in (inside), on (surface)

questions.q: I work ___ night and sleep ___ the afternoon.
questions.explanation: at, in. The exception: "at night" but "in the afternoon".

questions.q: We're ___ the bus and she's ___ bed.
questions.explanation: on, in. You travel on a bus; you are in bed.

questions.q: I'm sitting ___ you, on your right.

questions.explanation: at. Traffic lights are a point.

questions.q: We have a party ___ Christmas Day, but we give presents ___ Christmas.
questions.explanation: on, at. A specific day = on; the festival period = at.

questions.q: I work ___ night and sleep ___ the afternoon.
questions.explanation: at, in. The exception: "at night" but "in the afternoon".

questions.q: We're ___ the bus and she's ___ bed.
questions.explanation: on, in. You travel on a bus; you are in bed.

classes.title: Class 12: There is/are + there or it
classes.desc: There is / are; there was / were / Questions and negatives

questions.q: Make a question: "There is a bank near here."
options: Is there a bank near here?
questions.answer: Is there a bank near here?
questions.explanation: Is there a bank near here?

questions.q: "___ a pen and two books on the desk."
questions.explanation: There is. We match the first noun (a pen) in a list.
There. We say "there are" to say something exists.
It. The film was already named.

questions.q: ___ was a good film on TV last night.
questions.explanation: There. A new thing is introduced.

questions.q: How many people ___ there at the party?
Make a question: "There is a bank near here."
options: Is there a bank near here?
questions.answer: Is there a bank near here?
questions.explanation: Is there a bank near here?

questions.q: "___ a pen and two books on the desk."
questions.explanation: There is. We match the first noun (a pen) in a list.
There. We say "there are" to say something exists.

classes.title: Class 13: A/some/any + quantity words
classes.desc: Countable (apples) and uncountable (milk, advice) / some / any

questions.q: I have ___ friends in London, so I'm not alone.
questions.explanation: a few. "A few" is positive; "few" is almost none.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "I don't have many money."
questions.explanation: I don't have much money. "Money" is uncountable.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) an advice (b) some advice (c) advices
I need ___ sugar in my tea.
I have ___ friends in London, so I'm not alone.
questions.explanation: a few. "A few" is positive; "few" is almost none.

classes.title: Class 14: Was/were
classes.desc: Past of be: was/were / Negatives and questions

classes.title: Class 15: Past simple, regular and irregular verbs
classes.desc: Regular: -ed, -ied, doubled letter / Common irregular verbs

questions.explanation: visited. A stressed first syllable does not double the final letter.
read. It is spelled the same, pronounced /red/.

questions.q: Which -ed ending has a /t/ sound? (a) played (b) washed (c) wanted

questions.explanation: visited. A stressed first syllable does not double the final letter.
read. It is spelled the same, pronounced /red/.

classes.title: Class 16: Past simple, negatives and questions
classes.desc: didn't + base verb / Did + subject + base verb

questions.explanation: I wasn't there. "Be" does not use "didn't".
broke. When "who" is the subject there is no "did", and the verb is in past form.

questions.q: Which is correct? (a) Did she bought? (b) Did she buy? (c) Does she bought?

questions.explanation: I wasn't there. "Be" does not use "didn't".

classes.title: Class 17: Verbs + to/-ing + would like
classes.desc: want, need, hope, decide + to + infinitive / enjoy, like, love, hate, finish + -ing

questions.q: Which is a wish NOW? (a) I like swimming. (b) I'd like to swim.
Correct the sentence: "I want that you help me."
options: I want you to help me
questions.answer: I want you to help me
questions.explanation: I want you to help me.

questions.q: Which is a polite offer? (a) Do you like a coffee? (b) Would you like a coffee?
Which is a wish NOW? (a) I like swimming. (b) I'd like to swim.

classes.title: Class 18: Comparative and superlative adjectives
classes.desc: Short: -er / -est / Long: more / the most

questions.q: This is the ___ (bad) day of my life.
Which is correct? (a) more easy (b) easier (c) more easier
He is the ___ (fast) runner in the school.
Correct the sentence: "She is taller that me."
Which is correct? (a) the more important (b) the most important (c) the importantest
My new phone is ___ (good) than my old one.
This is the ___ (bad) day of my life.
Which is correct? (a) more easy (b) easier (c) more easier

classes.title: Class 19: Will/shall + be going to
classes.desc: will for quick decisions, promises, predictions / shall for offers/suggestions

questions.q: It's cold. I ___ close the window.
questions.explanation: will. It is a quick decision made now.

questions.q: I ___ see my uncle tomorrow. (I made the plan last week.)
questions.explanation: am going to. It is a plan made before.

questions.q: Look at the sky! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: is going to. There is evidence now (the sky).
Shall. It is an offer with I/we.

questions.q: Correct the sentence: "I will to go."

questions.explanation: will. It is a decision made at that moment.

questions.q: She ___ be a doctor. (She has decided.)
Which is correct? (a) Are you going visit? (b) Are you going to visit? (c) Do you going to visit?
It's cold. I ___ close the window.
questions.explanation: will. It is a quick decision made now.

questions.q: I ___ see my uncle tomorrow. (I made the plan last week.)
questions.explanation: am going to. It is a plan made before.

questions.q: Look at the sky! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: is going to. There is evidence now (the sky).
Shall. It is an offer with I/we.

classes.title: Class 20: Conjunctions + final review
classes.desc: and (adds), but (contrast), or (choice), so (result), because (reason) / To join short sentences

questions.q: It was cold, ___ I wore a coat.
questions.explanation: so. Cold is the reason; the coat is the result.

questions.q: I was late ___ the bus broke down.
questions.explanation: because. The bus breaking down is the reason.
or. After a negative, we use "or".

questions.q: She is poor ___ she is happy.
Which is correct? (a) He go to school yesterday and see his friends. (b) He went to school yesterday and saw his friends.
questions.explanation: (b). Both verbs must be in the past.

questions.q: Yesterday I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
questions.explanation: so. Tired is the reason; going to bed is the result.

questions.q: It was cold, ___ I wore a coat.
questions.explanation: so. Cold is the reason; the coat is the result.

questions.q: I was late ___ the bus broke down.
questions.explanation: because. The bus breaking down is the reason.
